verification_report.summary:
Bounded sequential verification of the supplied revision passes under the six explicitly accepted internal inputs. The entropy variational identity is valid for every Borel probability, including non-absolutely-continuous measures and infinite entropy, and for non-normalized smooth positive volume. The cutoff, truncation, Jensen and continuous-approximation arguments are valid.

Delta is a finite pseudometric on admitted model references. Its exact dual formula uses only the common finite-entropy domain, so no infinity-minus-infinity difference occurs. Bounded measurable scalar tests give the same supremum by applying L1 continuity separately to each fixed reference. Smooth-volume invariance follows from the independently established translation identity.

The stability gap is correctly bounded by 2 delta_j. Bounded delta_j places all supporting measures in one finite sublevel of the limiting dual, without a common smaller-background parameter. Uniform integrability controls the varying measurable tests, weak L1 convergence handles the fixed limiting test, and lower semicontinuity identifies every weak cluster point. A singleton supporting set gives full convergence in both stated weak senses.

Restricting every analytic-family parameter t to rational numbers in (0,1) repairs the stated convention mismatch. Ordinary equivalence from the analytic-envelope theorem, followed by bounded-change invariance, proves the model identity; ta supplies the genuine smaller-background competitor. No arbitrary-singularity envelope idempotence is assumed. The projective masses are (1-t)^n and the scalar differences are n log(1-t). Equality for rational t, and rational approximation from below for any fixed real epsilon, establish sharpness. On P^1 the multiplier ideals have exponent floor(mt), including integer endpoints, and distinct pole locations give different ordinary and ideal types at distance zero.

The proposed entropy substitutions and reuse of general stability in the zero-reference corollary introduce no circular dependency. Real epsilon_j remain allowed, with the original model and smaller-background hypotheses retained. The introductory phrase 'The preceding limit' should be adjusted to the proposed subsection placement; this is editorial only. No external-paper citation in the submitted proof requires a reference search. This report certifies the supplied rationally restricted revision within the stated scope, not the upstream inputs or a manuscript release. No stronger convergence, separation, completeness or novelty claim is accepted. Existing reports and manuscript files were left untouched.
